_comment: Year Journey events. Edit here, then run `npm run events` (scripts/build_events.py). Reviewed events carry `evidence`: each quote must appear in its source (keys in content/sources.json) and one quote (`date: true`) must give the date; a `mof-feio` row is checked against the Ministry of Finance's intervention data. Other events are matched automatically: one passage of a Wikipedia `sources` page (a sentence and the next) must contain the date and every keyword. Events in the featured years (1971, 1985, 1997, 2008, 2022) must be reviewed. Regions: USA CAN GBR DEU EA CHE IND CHN KOR JPN AUS. Currencies: slot ids (EUR = the Deutsche Mark before 1999) or USD. Summaries are our own short factual sentences; exchange-rate figures are computed by the app, never typed here. `precision` (month or year): the sources give only the month or the year; the app then shows no day, stops the year at no date and puts no marker on the chart.

events.title: The Deutsche Mark is born
events.summary: A currency reform replaces the Reichsmark with the Deutsche Mark in the western zones of Germany.

events.title: The yen is fixed at 360 per dollar
events.summary: Japan sets a single exchange rate of 360 yen to the US dollar, which holds until 1971.

events.title: Britain devalues the pound
events.summary: The pound is devalued by about 30%, to 2.80 dollars. Many other currencies follow within days.

events.title: Canada lets its dollar float
events.summary: Unlike the fixed currencies of the Bretton Woods system, the Canadian dollar is left to the market.

events.title: The Bundesbank is founded
events.summary: West Germany's new central bank, the Deutsche Bundesbank, takes over from the Bank deutscher Laender.

events.title: The Reserve Bank of Australia opens
events.summary: Australia's central banking moves to a new institution, the Reserve Bank of Australia.

events.title: The Mark is revalued
events.summary: West Germany raises the value of the Deutsche Mark against the dollar.

events.title: Canada fixes its dollar again
events.summary: Canada returns to a fixed rate, at 92.5 US cents.

events.title: The Australian dollar is introduced
events.summary: Australia switches to decimal currency: the Australian dollar replaces the Australian pound.

events.title: India devalues the rupee
events.summary: India lowers the official value of the rupee against the dollar.

events.title: Britain devalues the pound again
events.summary: The pound is devalued from 2.80 to 2.40 dollars.

events.title: The US asks to close the London gold market
events.summary: The United States asks Britain to close the London gold market the following day, to stop heavy demand for gold.

events.title: The Mark is revalued again
events.summary: West Germany raises the value of the Deutsche Mark against the dollar a second time.

events.title: Canada floats its dollar again
events.summary: As an inflation-fighting measure, Canada lets its dollar float once more.

events.title: The Mark floats
events.summary: When currency markets reopen on 10 May, West Germany lets the Mark float instead of holding its fixed rate.

evidence.quote: When foreign exchange markets reopened on May 10, the Mark was allowed to float

events.title: The dollar-gold break
events.summary: The United States suspends the convertibility of the dollar into gold. The fixed-rate system begins to break apart.

evidence.quote: Address to the Nation Outlining a New Economic Policy: "The Challenge of Peace." August 15, 1971

evidence.claim: The dollar's convertibility into gold is suspended
evidence.quote: suspend temporarily the convertibility of the dollar into gold or other reserve assets

evidence.claim: The fixed-rate system begins to break apart
evidence.quote: This was the end of the Bretton Woods international monetary system

events.title: Japan lets the yen float
events.summary: Two weeks after the US move, Japan stops holding the yen at 360 per dollar and lets it float.

evidence.quote: so that world currencies provisionally went into the floating exchange rate system (on August 28, for Japan)
The exchange rate of 360 yen per dollar, which started in 1949, also ended

events.title: The Smithsonian Agreement
events.summary: Meeting at the Smithsonian Institution in Washington, the Group of Ten agrees on new fixed rates: the dollar is devalued against gold, and the yen is set at 308 per dollar.

evidence.quote: an agreement was made at the Smithsonian Meeting (in Washington) on December 18
Remarks Announcing a Monetary Agreement Following a Meeting of the Group of Ten December 18, 1971

evidence.claim: The dollar is devalued against gold
evidence.quote: agreement by the United States to propose to the Congress a suitable means for devaluing the dollar in terms of gold

evidence.claim: The yen is set at 308 per dollar
evidence.quote: The Smithsonian Agreement in December 1971 devalued the yen parity by 16.88% to ¥308

events.title: Britain floats the pound
events.summary: Britain stops defending its fixed rate and lets the pound float.

events.title: The dollar falls again; the yen floats
events.summary: After a second devaluation of the dollar, Japan and much of Europe let their currencies float.

events.title: The oil price shock
events.summary: Gulf oil producers announce a sharp rise in the price of oil; production cuts and an embargo follow.

events.title: China begins reform and opening up
events.summary: A Communist Party meeting starts China's economic reforms and opening to the world.

events.title: The European Monetary System begins
events.summary: Several European countries agree to keep their currencies within bands against each other.

events.title: The Fed turns to fight inflation
events.summary: The Federal Reserve changes how it runs monetary policy to bring down high inflation; interest rates rise sharply.

events.title: Australia floats its dollar
events.summary: Australia lets the market set the value of its dollar.

events.title: The Plaza Accord
events.summary: Finance ministers and central bank governors of five major economies, meeting at the Plaza Hotel, say a further orderly rise of other currencies against the dollar is desirable.

evidence.quote: Ministers of Finance and Central Bank Governors of France, the Federal Republic of Germany, Japan. the United Kingdom, and the United States met today, September 22,1985
some further orderly appreciation of the main non-dollar currencies against the dollar is desirable
the finance ministers and central bank governors of the United States, France, Germany, Japan and Great Britain met at the Plaza Hotel in New York City

events.title: The Louvre Accord
events.summary: Six major economies agree to steady the dollar after its long fall.

events.title: Black Monday
events.summary: Stock markets around the world crash in a single day.

events.title: The Berlin Wall falls
events.summary: East Germany opens its border. Within a year the two German states unite.

events.title: German monetary union
events.summary: The Deutsche Mark becomes the currency of East Germany too, three months before unification.

events.title: Germany is reunified
events.summary: East and West Germany become one country.

events.title: Britain joins the ERM
events.summary: The pound joins Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism, which limits how far it may move against other European currencies.

events.title: India opens its economy
events.summary: In a balance-of-payments crisis, India's budget of 24 July begins wide economic reforms.

events.title: Black Wednesday
events.summary: Under heavy selling, Britain takes the pound out of the Exchange Rate Mechanism.

events.title: Thailand floats the baht
events.summary: Thailand moves the baht to a managed float, its value set by the market. The crisis that begins there spreads to other Asian economies, among them South Korea.

evidence.quote: Effective July 2, 1997

evidence.claim: The baht's value is set by the market
evidence.quote: to a managed float, with the value of the baht being determined by market forces
As the crisis spread, other Southeast Asian countries and later Japan and South Korea saw slumping currencies

events.title: Korea agrees an IMF rescue
events.summary: South Korea agrees a rescue program with the International Monetary Fund as the won falls.

evidence.claim: Talks concluded in Seoul on 3 December 1997
evidence.quote: Date and location: December 3, 1997, Seoul.
The IMF team and the Korean authorities concluded discussions on a strong economic program
The won depreciated by about 20 percent against the U.S. dollar through November 30

events.title: The European Central Bank is founded
events.summary: The European Central Bank replaces the European Monetary Institute, ready for the euro.

events.title: Russia defaults
events.summary: Russia devalues the ruble and defaults on its debt, unsettling markets worldwide.

events.title: The euro is launched
events.summary: Eleven countries adopt the euro for markets and banks; notes and coins follow in 2002.

events.title: Japan begins quantitative easing
events.summary: The Bank of Japan starts buying assets on a large scale to fight deflation.

events.title: Euro notes and coins arrive
events.summary: Euro banknotes and coins replace the national currencies in everyday use.

events.title: China loosens the yuan's peg
events.summary: China lifts the yuan's fixed peg to the dollar, with a one-time revaluation.

events.title: The credit crunch begins
events.summary: A large European bank freezes funds exposed to US mortgages, and lending between banks seizes up.

events.title: Lehman Brothers collapses
events.summary: The US financial firm Lehman Brothers files for bankruptcy protection.

evidence.quote: September 15, 2008 | SEC Filing: Lehman Brothers Holdings Inc. Lehman Brothers Holdings Incorporated files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection.
Lehman Brothers filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Monday, September 15, 2008

events.title: Central banks cut rates together
events.summary: Six central banks, among them the Federal Reserve and the European Central Bank, cut interest rates in a joint move.

evidence.quote: October 08, 2008 FOMC statement: Federal Reserve and other central banks announce reductions in policy interest rates
the Bank of Canada, the Bank of England, the European Central Bank, the Federal Reserve, Sveriges Riksbank, and the Swiss National Bank are today announcing reductions in policy interest rates

events.title: Switzerland caps the franc
events.summary: The Swiss National Bank sets a minimum of 1.20 francs per euro to stop the franc rising.

events.title: "Whatever it takes"
events.summary: The ECB's president says it will do whatever it takes to preserve the euro.

events.title: Japan's big monetary easing
events.summary: The Bank of Japan launches a new, much larger program of asset purchases.

events.title: The franc cap is dropped
events.summary: The Swiss National Bank abandons its minimum rate against the euro, and the franc jumps.

events.title: China devalues the yuan
events.summary: China changes how its daily reference rate is set, and the yuan falls by the most in two decades.

events.title: The Brexit vote
events.summary: The United Kingdom votes to leave the European Union, and the pound falls sharply.

events.title: US-China tariffs begin
events.summary: The United States and China put tariffs on each other's goods.

events.title: A pandemic is declared
events.summary: The World Health Organization declares COVID-19 a pandemic. Investors rush into dollars for a few weeks.

events.title: Russia invades Ukraine
events.summary: Russia launches a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, starting the largest war in Europe since the Second World War.

evidence.claim: Russia announces its operation on 24 February 2022
evidence.quote: Russia announces start of 'special military operation' 24 February 2022
On 24 February 2022, Russia invaded Ukraine, starting the largest and deadliest war in Europe since World War II

events.title: The Fed starts raising rates
events.summary: The Federal Reserve raises its target range for interest rates to 1/4 to 1/2 percent and expects further increases.

evidence.quote: March 16, 2022 Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 1/4 to 1/2 percent and anticipates that ongoing increases in the target range will be appropriate

events.title: Japan buys yen
events.summary: Japan's Ministry of Finance sells dollars and buys yen, 2.84 trillion yen in one day: its first purchase of yen since June 1998.

evidence.claim: 2,838.2 billion yen bought on 22 September 2022; the previous purchase of yen was on 17 June 1998

events.title: The UK mini-budget
events.summary: The UK announces large tax cuts that need more borrowing, with no independent forecast published. The pound falls sharply; by the next trading day it hits an all-time low against the dollar.

evidence.quote: The Chancellor of the Exchequer delivered his Growth Plan 2022 to Parliament on 23 September 2022
a sharp fall in the value of the pound sterling against the US dollar as world markets reacted negatively to the increased borrowing required

evidence.claim: No independent forecast; the all-time low
evidence.quote: no independent forecast by the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) had been published. By the next day of trading, the pound had hit an all-time low against the US dollar

events.title: Japan buys yen again
events.summary: Japan's Ministry of Finance buys yen again: 5.62 trillion yen on 21 October and 0.73 trillion yen on 24 October.

events.title: Silicon Valley Bank fails
events.summary: A large US bank collapses, and fears spread to other banks.

events.title: Japan ends negative interest rates
events.summary: The Bank of Japan ends its negative interest rate policy and yield curve control, and guides the overnight call rate to around 0 to 0.1 percent.

evidence.claim: the Bank of Japan's statement is dated 19 March 2024
evidence.quote: March 19, 2024 Bank of Japan Changes in the Monetary Policy Framework

evidence.claim: yield curve control and the negative interest rate policy end
evidence.quote: Quantitative and Qualitative Monetary Easing (QQE) with Yield Curve Control and the negative interest rate policy to date have fulfilled their roles

evidence.claim: the overnight call rate is guided to around 0 to 0.1 percent
evidence.quote: encourage the uncollateralized overnight call rate to remain at around 0 to 0.1 percent

events.title: Sweeping US tariffs
events.summary: The United States announces broad new tariffs on imports from most countries.

events.title: Japan and the US buy yen together
events.summary: Japan's Ministry of Finance buys yen in coordination with the US Treasury on 31 July (US Eastern Time). Over 30 July, 31 July and 3 August, Japan buys 15.4 trillion yen in all.

evidence.claim: The joint purchase on 31 July 2026 (US Eastern Time)
evidence.quote: On Friday 31st, July (U.S. Eastern Time), Japan's Ministry of Finance purchased the Japanese yen in coordination with the U.S. Department of the Treasury

evidence.claim: 1,871.4 billion yen bought on 3 August 2026 (15,399.3 billion over the three days)
